flags.detail: The repository's existing content (README, docs/, evidence/, scripts/) documents a DOE GEMS fault-prediction research project, which is unrelated to the current bathtub trip-lever brief. The bathtub project site occupies the repository root (what GitHub Pages serves from main). The legacy DOE GEMS evidence site remains under docs/ — its index page was temporarily overwritten by a parallel session's draft (PR #16) and was restored from git history during final integration on 2026-11-07.

source_links.label: Legacy GEMS evidence site preserved at docs/index.html

flags.title: All three estimates are owner-recorded; the amounts are not published
flags.detail: E-01, E-02 and E-03 are quotations recorded by the project owner from outreach dated 2026-08-30. No official source exists for a vendor's verbal or written quote, so per the project verification rule the dollar amounts are left blank on every served page and data file; the figures remain on file with the owner. The provider names were matched to licensed entities by name + San Francisco address + classification (official links in each row), but the owner must confirm these are the same businesses contacted. If the owner wants the three figures displayed on this site, request it against this flag and they will be published labeled owner-provided.

flags.title: The three quotes describe different scopes and are not directly comparable
flags.detail: E-03 is 'repair or adjust plunger handle'; E-02 is 'replace lever for the bathtub plug and spout with diverter, labor and materials'; E-01 is 'replacing waste and overflow' (full assembly). The amounts are on file with the owner and are not published (F-02). None of the three quotes explicitly includes drywall opening or ceiling restoration, which the fallback approach (working from below through a storage-unit ceiling) will likely require (R-06, R-07). Third-party guides put drywall patching at $300–$930 on top of plumbing work.

flags.title: CSLB statuses are point-in-time (data as of 2026-11-07)
flags.detail: License status was verified against official CSLB license-detail pages on 2026-11-06 and re-verified 2026-11-07 (final-integration session). CSLB states status 'can change at any time' and that its database may lag. Re-check each linked CSLB page before contracting. Worker's-comp notes: Bay Area Plumbing (#757796) and SF Building Group (#1106131) are WC-exempt (certified no employees); Fast Response's WC policy (#1024971) shows an expiration of 2026-12-18. Rapid Flow (#1115649) is also WC-exempt (certified no employees, effective 2026-02-03).

flags.title: No provider in the set holds a C-9 Drywall classification
flags.detail: None of the verified licenses includes C-9 (Drywall). The all-in-one requirement (R-07) is therefore satisfiable in two CSLB-sanctioned ways: (a) hire a B-licensed general contractor who contracts both the C-36 plumbing and a licensed C-9 drywall subcontractor under one contract (Ace #829071 and We Do Construction #1096552 hold B + C-36; SF Building Group #1106131 holds B), or (b) hire a C-36 plumber and separately contract a licensed drywall contractor. CSLB's official guidance: a B contractor is appropriate when a job requires more than two types of work and cannot legally contract for a single trade only.

source_links.label: CSLB — Find A Licensed Contractor (B vs C multi-trade guidance)

flags.title: Access-panel code section numbering differs across CPC editions
flags.detail: The 12-inch access requirement for concealed slip-joint connections (directly relevant to tub waste/overflow serviceability) is numbered 402.10 in the 2022 California Plumbing Code / UPC, but 404.2 in the 2010 CPC. Links to both editions are provided; the requirement text itself is consistent.

flags.title: Fast Response Plumbing & Rooter: CSLB address differs from website address
flags.detail: CSLB record of record for license #1024971 lists 236 W Portal Ave #459, San Francisco 94127; the company website displays 4444 Geary Blvd Ste 203, San Francisco 94118. Same license number and phone on both. Likely a mailing/office address difference; confirm at contract time.

flags.title: Review counts unknown for We Do Construction, SF Building Group, and Rapid Flow
flags.detail: No review counts or ratings could be captured for these three providers from the sources fetched this session. Per the verification rule, those cells are left blank rather than estimated. Ask both for references from occupied-unit jobs.

flags.title: Photos of the work area not yet available
flags.detail: The project owner states reference photos will be provided later; all analysis in this session is based on the written description only (R-12). Site access, tub type (alcove/freestanding), finish (tile/surround), and the storage-unit ceiling construction are unconfirmed and materially affect scope.

flags.title: Advanced Plumbing and Drain (#1009195): CSLB 'may be suspended at a future date' warning
flags.detail: The official CSLB record for license #1009195 (verified 2026-11-06) carries an Additional Status: 'The license may be suspended at a future date for failure to resolve an outstanding final liability from the Franchise Tax Board, Department of Industrial Relations, Employment Development Department, or the Contractors State License Board.' The license is currently active. Re-check the CSLB page immediately before any engagement.

flags.title: Duplicate public routes consolidated into this dashboard (resolved)
flags.detail: During final integration (2026-11-07) the parallel-session brief directories (bathtub-overflow/, bathroom-overflow/, trip-lever/, bathtub/, the docs/bathtub-* pages and the docs/bathtub-overflow/ stubs) were retired to redirect stubs pointing at this dashboard, making the repository root the single authoritative URL, as requested in the post-merge policy review (PR #18) and the standing canonical-URL request on the coordination board. No content was discarded: the full text of every brief remains in git history and in the closed pull-request threads (#8–#17, #21–#24). The record of the consolidation decision is in COORDINATION.md on GitHub.

flags.title: Canonical URL: the repository root is the project's single published site
flags.detail: This dashboard (repository root, served from main) is the only authoritative route for the bathtub trip-lever project. Former parallel routes now redirect here. The canonical URL is https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Korea8/ . The shared coordination board recording the multi-session work is COORDINATION.md in the repository.

flags.title: Third-party cost benchmarks and review figures are not official sources
flags.detail: Cost ranges from HomeGuide and Angi, and review counts/ratings from Yelp and similar platforms, are shown on this site only as clearly-labeled third-party context with links for manual re-checking; they are never badged 'verified'. The only cost figures this site treats as officially sourced are government fee schedules and the license/code/fee facts published by CSLB, sf.gov/DBI, IAPMO, and manufacturers. No official source publishes a price for this specific repair.

flags.title: Non-public project context is kept out of all served files
flags.detail: During final integration (2026-11-07), references to non-public project context were removed from every served file — pages, data files, and the coordination board — leaving only publicly verifiable material. Content committed before that date remains in git history and in the diff views of previously merged or closed pull requests; a history rewrite was deliberately not performed because it would break the shared branch and pull-request structure. The owner can request removal of specific historical content from GitHub if ever needed (GitHub documents this process for sensitive data in repositories).

source_links.label: GitHub Docs — removing sensitive data from a repository

flags.title: Source link-rot found and corrected during final-integration re-verification
flags.detail: During the 2026-11-07 line-by-line re-verification, three sources cited on 2026-11-06 stopped serving their content: IAPMO's 'Answers and Analysis' page (aa.iapmo.org) became members-only, and two Watco instruction PDF paths were removed in a site reorganization. All 11 CSLB license pages and all reachable provider sites were re-verified live on 2026-11-07 with matching data.
